note: Rewritten from the English description by Emerson (1956); the original is in English. Sjöstedt (1926) originally placed this species in Apicotermes, and Emerson moved it to Allognathotermes on the basis of a syntype soldier borrowed from the Natural History Museum, London, and a paratype soldier exchanged from the Stockholm museum. The soldier measurement table in the original is entirely mirrored and garbled in the scan (e.g. "eIqi} pury Jo y43ua]") and cannot be reliably restored, so no measurements are adopted here; type locality Aburi, Gold Coast.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The most conspicuous species-level character lies in the anterior margin of the pronotum: in A. hypogeus and A. ivorensis the median notch is narrower and pointed, with the two anterior peaks approaching each other directly in front; in this species the notch is wider and not pointed, the two peaks are farther apart, and the notch angle is about 135°. The head is longer than in A. hypogeus, the sides straighter, and it narrows anteriorly in a manner close to A. ivorensis. The first marginal tooth of the left mandible is smaller than in A. hypogeus and forms a much flatter and broader angle with the apical cutting edge; A. hypogeus and A. ivorensis resemble each other in this respect. The postmentum is longer than in A. hypogeus, with the sides between the anterior part and the constriction straighter; the width at the constriction equals that of the Adiopodoumé specimens of A. hypogeus and is clearly less constricted than in the paratype soldier or in the figure given for A. ivorensis. The fore coxa is almost identical to that of A. hypogeus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pilosity approaches that of A. hypogeus, but the setae on the posterior part of the vertex are not as long as in the latter. The head is longer than in A. hypogeus, the sides straighter, narrowing anteriorly. Antennae 14-segmented. Mandibles approach those of A. hypogeus. The postmentum is longer than in A. hypogeus, the sides straighter; in the paratype soldier the section of the postmentum before the constriction is about 1/8 of the postmentum length measured from the middle of the posterior margin. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a broad, non-pointed median notch, the two peaks far apart, the notch angle about 135°.
